edits.before: Week 7 cites this for the thing it gets wrong on its own. The lecture separates overload, shutdown and burnout, and says openly that only burnout has a research definition behind it. This paper shows that **shutdown is a named phenomenon in the literature**, not the course's coinage — and that the literature names two more the course's taxonomy omits entirely, **inertia** and **meltdown**. The sample is eight children and youth, so nothing here is a claim about adults or about prevalence; what it supports is that the course's three scales are an incomplete map, and the week now says so.
edits.after: Week 7's planning model separates overload, shutdown and burnout. This paper discusses **shutdown** and also names **inertia** and **meltdown**, which the model omits. The sample is eight children and youth; this annotation makes no claim about adults or prevalence. The course's three time scales are an incomplete map.
